scenes.text: You're halfway up a hill, standing on the pedals, your legs are already burning, and the bike keeps slowing down.
A lower gear changes the math. One pedal turn moves the bike a shorter distance, so each push asks for less force.
You trade speed for effort you can sustain. The climb feels steadier, your breathing settles, and your pedals keep turning.
Shift to an easier gear before the climb, while your pedals are turning lightly on the flat. Don't wait until you're straining.
